title: Scott Bessent 'May Have Overplayed His Hand'
summary: Bond bears are pushing benchmark Treasury yields toward the closely-watched 5% level ahead of US inflation data that stands to determine expectations for a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike next week. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent dismissed concerns about the US bond market after Thursday's smaller-than-expected debt buyback operation sent yields to multi-year highs. The Treasury market is in "very good shape," Bessent said in an interview with Steve Bannon. Speaking to Caroline Hepker and Francine Lacqua on Bloomberg Radio Julien Lafargue, Chief Market Strategist at Barclays Private Bank said that Bessent may have overplayed his hand. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: The Man Spending $70,000 To Play 100 Top US Golf Courses

title: India FX Deposits to Help Earn More Revenue, RBI’s Malhotra Says
summary: India’s central bank rejected estimates that its record foreign-currency deposit drive will prove costly, saying the inflows will instead generate additional income for the Reserve Bank of India as it deploys the dollars overseas, Governor Sanjay Malhotra said Friday.

title: Efron: Iran War Solved None of Israel’s Problems
summary: The UN's atomic watchdog IAEA says it has observed construction activity at Iran's Pickaxe Mountain. That's after President Trump drew attention to the suspected nuclear site in public comments at least twice in the last week. Shira Efron, Distinguished Chair for Israel Policy at RAND spoke to Bloomberg’s Abeer Abu Omar about the activity in Iran and what this means for Israel especially as election looms in the country. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: IEA Cuts Its Forecast for Oil Demand

title: Neko Health CEO: Using AI Scans & Longitudinal Data for a Longer Life
summary:
The CEO of full-body scanner Neko Health says technology could help shift healthcare from treating symptoms to identifying risks earlier.
Hjalmar Nilsonne explains how Neko’s scans combine imaging, cardiovascular testing and blood analysis to build a detailed picture of a person’s health, while repeated scans can create longitudinal data to track changes and uncover deeper patterns over time. Nilsonne predicts that in his lifetime AI and more personalized medicine could ultimately help people stay healthier for longer. He spoke to Tom Mackenzie on the latest episode of "Bloomberg Tech: Europe." (Source: Bloomberg)
